tasks.title: Add rate limiting and input sanitization to API endpoints
tasks.description: Implement a request‑rate‑limiting middleware (e.g., express‑rate‑limit) in server.js to protect public endpoints from brute‑force and DoS attacks. Add a validation layer using a schema library (e.g., Joi) in src/lib/db.js and route handlers to sanitize and validate all incoming parameters (search queries, booking dates, user IDs). This prevents injection attacks and ensures only well‑formed data reaches the database.
acceptance: Requests exceeding 100 per minute from the same IP receive HTTP 429 responses.
All API payloads are validated against defined Joi schemas; malformed requests return HTTP 400 with a clear error message.
No SQL injection or XSS payload can be persisted in the database (verified with automated security tests).

tasks.title: Introduce DB connection pooling and in‑memory caching for listings
tasks.description: Refactor src/lib/db.js to use a connection pool (e.g., pg‑pool for PostgreSQL) instead of creating a new client per request, reducing latency and resource usage. Add a simple LRU cache (e.g., node‑cache) for the most‑requested listings (GET /listings) and search results, with a TTL of 5 minutes. Update server.js to serve cached data when available and fall back to the DB otherwise.
acceptance: Database connections are reused; the number of active connections never exceeds the pool size (e.g., 20).
Cache hit rate for listings is at least 60% in load tests.
Response time for GET /listings drops by ≥30% compared to baseline (measured with a simple load test).

tasks.title: Interactive Map Clustering for Listings
tasks.description: Add a clustering layer to the map view so that when many listings are displayed the markers are grouped into clusters. Use the Supercluster library to compute clusters client‑side based on the current map bounds and zoom level. Extend src/components/MapView.jsx to import the new clustering utility, render cluster markers with a count badge, and zoom into the cluster bounds on click. Create src/lib/mapClusterEngine.js that exposes a function `getClusters(listings, viewport, zoom)` returning GeoJSON features for both clusters and individual listings. Ensure the map updates efficiently on pan/zoom and that clicking a cluster smoothly animates to the appropriate zoom level. Update any related CSS for cluster marker styling.
acceptance: When the map is zoomed out, listings are displayed as cluster markers showing the number of listings in that area.
Clicking a cluster marker zooms the map to a level where the cluster expands into smaller clusters or individual listing markers.
Performance test with 1,000 listings shows map interactions (pan, zoom) remain smooth (no frame drops below 30 fps).

tasks.title: Real‑time Chat Messaging via WebSocket
tasks.description: Add a WebSocket layer to the existing chat system so that messages are delivered instantly to all participants. Implement a lightweight chat engine (src/lib/chatEngine.js) that persists messages in SQLite and emits events through socket.io. Extend server.js to initialize a Socket.io server, register connection handlers, and integrate with existing insertMessage / getMessagesForListing functions. Update the front‑end components ChatModal.jsx and InboxModal.jsx to open a socket connection, listen for incoming messages, and update the UI state without a page refresh. Ensure fallback to the existing REST/GraphQL API for initial load and for browsers without WebSocket support.
acceptance: When a user sends a message in a listing chat, the other participant sees the new message instantly in the UI without reloading the page.
All sent messages are persisted in the SQLite database and are loaded correctly after a full page refresh.

tasks.title: Push Notification Engine for Real‑time Guest & Host Alerts
tasks.description: Implement a web‑push notification system that alerts guests and hosts about booking lifecycle events. Add a new module `src/lib/notifications.js` that wraps the `web-push` library, generates VAPID keys, and provides `saveSubscription(userId, subscription)`, `sendNotification(userId, payload)` helpers. Extend `src/lib/db.js` with a `notifications` table (id, userId, endpoint, keys, createdAt) and CRUD functions. Create a new Express route `POST /api/notifications/subscribe` in `server.js` that validates the JWT, stores the subscription, and returns success. Hook into the booking mutation (`addBooking` in `src/lib/graphqlResolvers.js`) to call `sendNotification` for the guest and host when a booking is confirmed, cancelled, or refunded. On the frontend, add `src/components/PushNotificationProvider.jsx` that requests Notification permission, registers the service worker, and posts the subscription to the new endpoint. Also add `src/components/NotificationToast.jsx` that listens for `push` events via the service worker and displays a toast using a UI library. Ensure the service worker file `public/sw.js` is served and can show notifications when the app is in background. Update the UI to include a bell icon in the Navbar that shows unread count and opens a list of recent notifications.
acceptance: Granting permission in the browser stores a subscription record in the `notifications` table and returns HTTP 200.
When a booking is confirmed, the guest receives a web‑push notification (visible in the browser) and a toast appears in the UI.
The bell icon in the Navbar updates its badge count after a new notification is received.
If the user revokes permission, the subscription endpoint returns a 403 and the stored subscription is removed.

tasks.title: Host Payout & Revenue Analytics Dashboard
tasks.description: Implement a new analytics dashboard for hosts that shows payout history, upcoming payouts, and revenue breakdown per listing. Add a new GraphQL query `hostRevenueAnalytics(hostId: ID!): RevenueAnalytics!` returning total earnings, earnings by month, pending payouts, and average occupancy rate. Create resolver in `src/lib/graphqlResolvers.js` and data fetchers in `src/lib/db.js` using parameterized queries and aggregation. Add a new React component `src/components/HostPayoutAnalytics.jsx` that fetches the data via Apollo client, displays charts using a lightweight chart library (e.g., Chart.js), and integrates with existing `HostDashboard`. Secure the endpoint with auth middleware and ensure only the host can access their own data. Update `server.js` to register the new resolver and add rate limiting for the analytics query.
acceptance: Authenticated host can open the Host Dashboard and see a new 'Payout & Revenue' tab displaying a chart of monthly earnings and a table of pending payouts.
GraphQL query `hostRevenueAnalytics` returns correct aggregated values for a host with multiple listings, verified by comparing against raw DB data.
Unauthenticated or other‑host users receive an authorization error when attempting to query `hostRevenueAnalytics`.
Rate limiting middleware rejects requests exceeding 10 queries per minute per host IP.

tasks.title: Instant Booking Approval Flow
tasks.description: Add a host‑driven approval step for instant‑book listings. Extend the bookings table with a new `approvalStatus` column (pending, approved, rejected). Implement a GraphQL mutation `approveBooking(id: ID!, approve: Boolean!): Booking` that updates the column and triggers a notification. Update the booking engine to respect `approvalStatus` when calculating availability and generating payment intents. In the Host Dashboard UI, add a new "Pending Approvals" tab that lists pending instant‑book bookings with Approve/Reject buttons, calling the mutation. Ensure the BookingWidget disables the "Book now" button for listings with `instantBook = 0` or when the host has disabled auto‑approval. Add server‑side validation to prevent unauthorized users from approving bookings.
acceptance: A new `approvalStatus` column exists in the `bookings` table and defaults to 'pending' for instant‑book reservations.
The GraphQL schema includes a `approveBooking` mutation that updates the status and returns the updated booking object.
Host Dashboard shows a "Pending Approvals" section listing only bookings with `approvalStatus = 'pending'` and allows the host to approve or reject each.
When a booking is approved, the booking becomes visible to the guest and a payment request is generated; when rejected, the booking is cancelled and the guest receives a notification.
The BookingWidget prevents guests from booking a listing that is not instant‑book enabled or that requires host approval, displaying an appropriate message.

tasks.title: iCal Calendar Availability Sync for Listings
tasks.description: Add bi‑directional iCal synchronization for listing availability. Implement a new Express route GET /api/calendar/:listingId.ics that generates a valid iCal feed containing all booked dates for the given listing. Add a POST /api/calendar/:listingId/sync endpoint that accepts an external iCal URL, parses events, and creates corresponding blocked bookings in the DB. Extend the GraphQL schema with a `listingCalendarSync` field (status, externalUrl) and mutations `setCalendarSyncUrl` and `removeCalendarSync`. Create a new backend module src/lib/calendarSync.js handling iCal generation, parsing (using  node-ical library), and DB updates. Add a UI component src/components/CalendarSyncWidget.jsx that lets hosts view current sync status, set an external iCal URL, and download their own iCal feed. Update host dashboard to include the widget. Ensure proper validation, error handling, and caching of generated feeds for 5 minutes.
acceptance: GET /api/calendar/:listingId.ics returns a 200 response with Content‑Type text/calendar and contains VEVENT entries for each confirmed booking of the listing.

POST /api/calendar/:listingId/sync with a valid iCal URL creates blocked bookings that prevent overlapping reservations, verified by attempting to book a conflicting date and receiving a conflict error.
The CalendarSyncWidget shows the current sync status, allows setting/removing an external iCal URL, and displays a download button that triggers the GET iCal endpoint.
GraphQL query listing(id: $id) { calendarSync { status externalUrl } } returns correct sync information after mutations.

tasks.title: Multi‑currency Checkout Support
tasks.description: Implement end‑to‑end multi‑currency checkout. Add a currency selector UI component and persist the user’s preferred currency in a cookie. Extend src/lib/currencyEngine.js to fetch live FX rates from a public API (e.g., exchangerate.host) and cache them for 10 minutes. Update all price‑related calculations (bookingEngine, pricingEngine, couponEngine) to accept a currency argument and convert amounts using the cached rates. Modify the GraphQL schema to expose a `currency` field on Listing, Booking and Payment types and add resolvers that return prices in the user’s selected currency. Update the payment integration in src/lib/iyzicoEngine.js to send the correct `currency` parameter in the request payload. Adjust src/components/PaymentModal.jsx and src/components/BookingWidget.jsx to display prices in the selected currency and to pass the currency to the backend when creating a booking. Ensure that the server validates the currency code against an allowed list and sanitizes the input.
acceptance: A currency selector appears on the listing detail page; selecting EUR updates all displayed prices (nightly, fees, total) to EUR with correct conversion.
The GraphQL query for a booking returns a `currency` field and all monetary fields are converted to the requested currency.
When a user confirms a booking in EUR, the request to iyzico contains `currency: "EUR"` and the amount matches the converted total.
Invalid or unsupported currency codes are rejected with a 400 response and a clear error message.

tasks.title: Guest Review Moderation Dashboard
tasks.description: Add a moderation workflow for guest reviews. Extend the SQLite schema with a `status` column (enum: pending, approved, rejected) and a `flagReason` text field in the `reviews` table. Update DB helper functions to create, fetch, and update review status. Add GraphQL types and mutations: `flagReview(id, reason)`, `moderateReview(id, action)` where action is APPROVE or REJECT. Implement a new React admin component `AdminReviewModeration` that lists reviews with status 'pending', shows the flag reason, and provides Approve/Reject buttons. The component should call the GraphQL mutations, refresh the list, and display success/error toasts. Secure the endpoint with `authMiddleware` ensuring only users with role `admin` can access. Add unit tests for the resolver and integration test for the UI flow.
acceptance: Admin user can view a list of pending reviews with flag reasons in the AdminReviewModeration UI.
Clicking Approve changes the review status to 'approved' and removes it from the pending list.
Clicking Reject changes the review status to 'rejected' and removes it from the pending list.
GraphQL mutations return the updated review object and appropriate error messages for unauthorized users.
All new DB columns are populated correctly and persisted across server restarts.

tasks.title: AI‑Powered Personalized Listing Recommendations
tasks.description: Implement a recommendation engine that suggests listings to a guest based on their past bookings, search history, and similar user behavior. Add a new GraphQL query `recommendedListings(userId: ID!, limit: Int = 10): [Listing]` that returns a ranked list of listings. Create a server‑side module `src/lib/recommendationEngine.js` that uses SQLite queries and a simple collaborative‑filtering algorithm (e.g., user‑based similarity on booking categories). Extend `server.js` to register the resolver. Build a frontend carousel component `src/components/RecommendationCarousel.jsx` that fetches the data via the GraphQL query and displays cards with lazy‑loaded images. Insert the carousel into the home page (`src/App.jsx`) under the “Explore” section. Ensure the new endpoint is protected by existing auth middleware and respects rate limiting.
acceptance: GraphQL query `recommendedListings` returns at most `limit` listings and includes fields `id`, `title`, `pricePerNight`, `images`.
When a logged‑in user opens the home page, the recommendation carousel appears with at least one listing card and scrolls horizontally.
Recommendations differ between two users with distinct booking histories, demonstrating personalization.
No new security warnings appear in the audit report; rate limiting headers are present on the GraphQL endpoint.

tasks.title: Lazy‑load and serve responsive images
tasks.description: Update all image components (e.g., ListingCard, ListingDetail, ExperienceCard) to use with appropriate width descriptors. Add a fallback placeholder and ensure images adapt to device pixel ratio. Improves initial page load and mobile UX.
acceptance: Images are not fetched until they enter the viewport (verified via network tab).
Different image sizes are served based on screen width and DPR (checked with srcset attribute).
Page load time (TTFB) improves by at least 15% on mobile devices.

tasks.title: Add CSRF protection to state‑changing endpoints
tasks.description: Integrate the existing csrfMiddleware into the Express pipeline for all POST/PUT/DELETE routes (including /graphql). Generate a CSRF token on authentication, store it in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, and require the token in the 'x-csrf-token' header. Reject requests missing or with an invalid token with 403. Update authMiddleware to set the cookie flags (secure in production, httpOnly, sameSite).
acceptance: A CSRF token is set as a cookie after login and can be read via generateCsrfToken()
POST/PUT/DELETE requests without the x-csrf-token header are responded with 403
Valid token requests succeed and the cookie has HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure (in prod) flags

tasks.title: Enforce strict input validation and sanitization for listings and bookings
tasks.description: Use the existing Joi schemas (listingSchema, bookingSchema) in the request handlers for creating/updating listings and bookings. Replace the simple HTML regex strip with a robust library (e.g., DOMPurify) to prevent XSS, and enforce length limits on strings. Return 400 with clear error messages on validation failure.
acceptance: Creating or updating a listing with HTML tags results in stripped content, not stored raw
Requests with missing required fields or invalid types are rejected with 400 and a Joi error message
All mutation endpoints (e.g., insertListing, insertBooking) now validate payloads before DB insertion

tasks.title: Set secure cookie attributes for auth tokens
tasks.description: Configure the authentication cookie to include HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict flags. Update the token generation logic in src/lib/auth.js and the cookie middleware in server.js to use these options. This prevents client‑side script access and mitigates CSRF and session hijacking attacks.
acceptance: Set‑Cookie header contains HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict for all authentication cookies
Browser devtools show the cookie as inaccessible to JavaScript
Existing login flow works without errors after the change

tasks.title: Enforce HTTP Strict Transport Security
tasks.description: Add the Strict-Transport-Security header via Helmet to force browsers to use HTTPS for all future requests, include subdomains and the preload flag. This protects against protocol downgrade attacks and cookie hijacking.
acceptance: All HTTPS responses include the 'Strict-Transport-Security' header with max-age>=31536000, includeSubDomains, and preload
Curl request to https endpoint returns the HSTS header
Browser console shows no mixed‑content warnings after enabling HSTS

tasks.title: Migrate all DB access to prepared statements
tasks.description: Replace any raw string concatenation used in `src/lib/db.js` with parameterized queries using `better-sqlite3`'s `prepare`, `run`, `get`, and `all` methods. Ensure every function that interacts with the database (e.g., insertListing, updateBookingStatus, getUserByEmail, etc.) uses bound parameters to prevent SQL injection and improve query planning. Add unit tests that attempt injection payloads and verify they are safely escaped.
acceptance: All DB functions use `db.prepare(...).run(...)` or `.get(...)` with placeholders
Injection attempts (e.g., "' OR 1=1 --") are rejected or result in no data leakage
Existing functionality (CRUD operations) continues to work as before

tasks.title: Add GraphQL query depth limiting
tasks.description: Integrate a depth‑limiting middleware (e.g., graphql-depth-limit) into the GraphQL handler to reject queries exceeding a configurable depth (e.g., 8). This prevents maliciously crafted deep queries from exhausting CPU and memory, mitigating DoS attacks.
acceptance: Requests with query depth > 8 receive a 400 response with an error message.
Normal queries (depth ≤ 8) continue to work unchanged.
Performance tests show no noticeable latency increase for valid queries.

tasks.title: Implement refresh‑token rotation and revocation list
tasks.description: Modify the authentication flow to issue a short‑lived access token and a refresh token that is stored hashed in the database. On each token refresh, invalidate the previous refresh token and store the new one, adding the old token to a revocation list. This mitigates token replay and stolen‑token attacks.
acceptance: Refresh endpoint returns a new access token and a new refresh token.
Using an old refresh token after rotation results in a 401 error.
Revoked tokens are persisted and checked on each refresh request.

tasks.title: GraphQL Query Complexity Limiting
tasks.description: Integrate graphql-query-complexity (or similar) into the GraphQL middleware to calculate a complexity score for each incoming query and reject queries that exceed a configurable threshold (e.g., 200). This prevents abuse via overly deep or wide queries that could degrade performance.
acceptance: Complexity middleware is applied to the GraphQL endpoint.
Queries with complexity > 200 receive a 400 response with an error message.
Normal queries (e.g., fetching a listing with its reviews) succeed unchanged.

tasks.title: Authentication Endpoint Rate Limiting & Lockout
tasks.description: Add a dedicated rate limiter for login, registration, and token refresh endpoints. Limit to 5 attempts per IP per minute and lock the user account for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts. Store attempt counters in memory or a fast cache (e.g., Redis) and reset on successful login. Return appropriate 429 responses with a clear message.
acceptance: More than 5 login attempts from the same IP within a minute receive HTTP 429.
A user with 10 consecutive failed logins receives a lockout response and cannot log in for 15 minutes.
Successful login resets the failure counter.

tasks.title: Add cursor‑based pagination for listings and bookings APIs
tasks.description: Implement cursor‑based pagination (limit, after) in the database query layer for listings, bookings, and related GraphQL resolvers. Return a pageInfo object with hasNextPage and endCursor. This reduces payload size and improves response time for large data sets.
acceptance: API accepts ?limit= and&after=cursor parameters and returns paginated results
GraphQL query for listings supports arguments (limit: Int, after: String) and returns edges + pageInfo
Performance test shows reduced response payload size for >1000 listings

tasks.title: Per‑user/IP rate limiting for booking and payment endpoints
tasks.description: Create a dedicated rate limiter (e.g., 5 requests per minute) for high‑risk actions such as '/api/bookings', '/api/payments', and related GraphQL mutations. Tie the limiter to the authenticated user ID and the client IP to prevent brute‑force or abuse while allowing normal usage.
acceptance: Requests exceeding the limit receive HTTP 429 with a clear error message
Legitimate users can still create bookings/payments within the allowed threshold
Rate limiting logs are emitted for monitoring and debugging

tasks.title: Batch GraphQL data fetching with DataLoader
tasks.description: Introduce DataLoader instances for users, listings, and reviews in the GraphQL resolvers to batch and cache database calls, eliminating N+1 query problems and reducing SQLite load. Update src/lib/graphqlResolvers.js and src/lib/db.js to use the new loaders.
acceptance: GraphQL queries that request nested fields (e.g., listing.author, listing.reviews) result in a single batched SQL statement per type.
Performance benchmarks show at least a 30% reduction in query count and response time for typical listing detail requests.

tasks.title: Real‑time Booking Updates via GraphQL Subscriptions
tasks.description: Add GraphQL subscription support so hosts and guests receive live updates when a booking status changes. Install graphql-ws, create a WebSocket server in server.js, extend the GraphQL schema with a `bookingUpdated` subscription, implement resolver that publishes to a PubSub instance when `updateBookingStatus` is called. Update the client side (e.g., src/components/BookingWidget.jsx) to open a subscription using @apollo/client's `useSubscription` hook and display a toast notification. Ensure authentication middleware validates the token for subscription connections.
acceptance: When a booking status is changed via the existing mutation, a `bookingUpdated` event is published and the subscribed client receives the new status within 2 seconds.
The UI shows a toast notification in the host dashboard and guest view without a page reload.

tasks.title: Faceted Search and Filter Engine
tasks.description: Add a faceted search system that lets users filter listings by price range, amenities, rating, and location. Implement a new GraphQL query `searchListings(filter: SearchFilter, pagination: PaginationInput): ListingConnection` with a resolver in server.js that uses a parameterized SQL builder in a new module `src/lib/searchEngine.js`. The engine will construct safe WHERE clauses and leverage DataLoader for batch loading of related data (e.g., amenities). Create a UI filter panel component `src/components/FacetedSearch.jsx` and modify `src/components/ListingGrid.jsx` to accept filter props and request filtered data via the new GraphQL query. Validate filter inputs with Joi in `src/lib/searchEngine.js` and ensure all queries use prepared statements to prevent injection.
acceptance: Selecting a price range and one or more amenities updates the listing grid to show only listings that match all selected criteria.
The GraphQL `searchListings` query returns a correct totalCount and a paginated list of listings matching the filter, verified by a GraphQL Playground test.
All SQL statements generated by the search engine use parameterized queries; attempts to inject SQL via filter fields are safely escaped and do not affect the query.
The filter UI remains responsive, with the filtered results rendering in under 200 ms for a dataset of 1,000 listings.
